problem_type: A node's versions (main pointer + history) had several hand-copied owners, so version order, version numbers and the timing of physical file deletion could drift or lose data
symptom: Version labels used the list index and shifted on every add or delete; setting an older version as main and generating again reordered the list; deleting a version removed its file immediately so undo restored an empty card; a version file still played by the timeline was deleted with the version.
direct_cause: Three separate history mergers (run outcome, local image edit, whiteboard snapshot) each re-derived result identity and moved the current pointer to the front; removal moved the next main to the front; deleteAssetResult deleted the file right after saving; the deferred-deletion draft used its own substring reference check and flushed everything on app close; set-main went through a bare updateNode with no undo step and rollbackHistory duplicated it as an untested runtime action.
class_root: The node-version lifecycle (append, number, set main, remove, delete file) had no single owner, and the question 'is this project file still referenced' had two implementations.
affected_population: Every node with two or more versions (image, video, edited image, whiteboard snapshot)
Legacy projects whose versions have no number or whose main pointer is an older version
Any project where a version is deleted while undo can still bring it back, or where the timeline uses that version
entry_points: appendNodeResultVersion (run outcome, image edit, whiteboard snapshot)
removeNodeResult via deleteAssetResult (node tray, asset library)
pendingAssetDeletions: undo eviction, project release, project open sweep
internal_only_reason: Version numbering, undo-journal reachability and project file references are application-owned invariants; no third-party library decides them.
invariants: history is the durable newest-first order: appending inserts at the front, removing only removes, setting main only moves the result pointer.
Each version carries a versionNo that never changes once assigned; a new version gets max + 1; legacy versions are numbered once on open (oldest = 1) and written back.

A loaded-project deletion is one undo step; its file is deleted only after the undo journal can no longer reach that step, on project release, or on the next project open, and only if neither the canvas nor the timeline still references the file.
Pending deletions are saved in the same project write that removes the version, so an abrupt exit cannot lose track of them.

door_reduction.why_not: Three different producers (generation outcome, local image edit, whiteboard snapshot) genuinely create versions and all call the one append owner; the two reference-check doors are the plan (decide at deletion time) and the pending queue (decide again when the file is due) calling the same predicate; set-main has one read and one write door in the only UI that offers it.

generality_proof: Every way a version enters, leaves or becomes main goes through nodeResultLifecycle.ts (the three hand-copied mergers and rollbackNodeHistory are deleted), and every physical deletion of a version file goes through isProjectFileReferenced, either in the plan or in the pending queue. A new producer cannot append without numbering because the only append function numbers, and a new deletion path cannot skip the timeline because the only reference check includes it.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Number a new version max + 1, insert it at the front and keep the durable order; normalize legacy numbers first without renumbering existing ones.
Hold a deleted version's file until its undo step is unreachable, the project is released, or the project is reopened; persist the queue with the project.
The single answer to whether a project file is still used by any canvas version or timeline clip.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Crop / grid / transform / remove-background results used a private mergeNodeImageHistory; now call the shared append.
Whiteboard snapshots used a private mergeWhiteboardSnapshotHistory plus an inline array; both now call the shared append.
Asset library deletion calls the shared deletion boundary and therefore the deferred queue.
Alt-drag copy strips the source version number and names the card by version number instead of list index.
Creates a brand-new node with a single fresh result; the first append or open backfill numbers it.

recurrence.reason: Any producer added later, any legacy project, and any deletion followed by more gestures or an abrupt exit can hit the same mechanisms.
same_class_scan: rg "history:\s*\[|\.history\s*=" src (found three hand-copied mergers and one inline whiteboard array)
rg rollbackHistory src electron tests (no production caller; deleted)

prevention.invariant: No code outside nodeResultLifecycle.ts builds a node history from another history; no code deletes a version file without isProjectFileReferenced.
prevention.failure_mode: An unnumbered or duplicate-numbered version is numbered max + 1 instead of renumbering others; a pending deletion whose step is still reachable stays queued; a referenced file is written off without deletion.
prevention.strategy: Delete the private mergers and the duplicate set-main action, route producers through one append, and make the deferred queue durable and reference-checked.

legacy_paths.rationale: Removed second owners of the same lifecycle step: mergeResultHistory (nodeRunOutcome.ts), mergeNodeImageHistory (useNodeImageEditing.ts), mergeWhiteboardSnapshotHistory (WhiteboardModal.tsx), rollbackNodeHistory (graphOps.ts), rollbackHistory (canvasRunActions.ts), and the pagehide flush that deleted still-undoable files (workbenchProjectSession.ts).

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency controls the lifecycle invariant.

migration: On project open, versions without a number are numbered once from the durable order (oldest = 1) and saved with the existing open-time migration write. The optional payload field pendingAssetDeletions is read on open and swept; older builds ignore it.
residual_risks: Ctrl+Z replays the journal prefix, so an undo after a generation landed can hide that landed result (pre-existing, outside this change; reported to the coordinator).
Pending deletions are released against the canvas and timeline only; other future consumers of result URLs must join isProjectFileReferenced.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The lifecycle model owns version order and numbering; the pending queue owns file timing and is proven with the real canvas store and undo journal.
